# Session dispatch + babysitting (OpenChamber program)

## Purpose
Move the fleet's larger code work off Claude cron shifts — whose every turn re-buys a large context — onto OpenChamber-hosted OpenCode sessions running on plan pools, watched by ONE babysitter worker instead of one worker per issue. Design record: `openchamber-dispatch-babysitter-design-2026-10-26.md` (keep-the-four-repos-healthy goal workspace, files/).

## Scope
- **Locations abstraction:** a session executor is a location (kind: openchamber | opencode-server | openclaw | codex-aster) with an adapter + capacity, so more OpenChamber machines, an OpenClaw gateway, or a Codex `.aster` route plug in without changing the babysitter loop. First location: the laptop's OpenChamber.
- **Dispatcher with admission control:** hands queue tasks marked `executor: openchamber` to sessions only when a slot is free and the routed pool passes the quota measurement gate; otherwise hands the task back (parked `executor-saturated`, noted on the issue) — never a silent backlog.
- **One babysitter:** rounds over every bound session — progress verdicts, one stall nudge then escalation, quota walls as named parks, harvesting finished sessions into verified terminal queue states. Reports quota per pool and a routing ledger (pool used per session, escalations, burn per landed task).
- **Routing, Workhorse-first:** Fast / Workhorse (default) / Frontier tiers per the POOL MAP; Frontier only on evidence or for the design half of a split

# Design mill: one fleet surface for OpenCode, OpenChamber, ID, and mcpx

Drew's design, dictated 2026-11-14. Protected design — do not close or drop without Drew.

## The idea in plain words

All automation and agent calls to OpenChamber, OpenCode, the ID binary, and the mcpx binary should go through subcommands of the fleet binary. At first this is mostly pass-through to the same underlying binary/endpoint, but fleet automatically resolves WHERE to talk: the right port on localhost, the right socket, the right endpoint path for that service on that host. Credentials are populated automatically and the caller can skip those fields. A raw mode (explicit endpoint path, raw POST body, explicit flag) always exists as an override.

This is a design mill with multiple passes, not one build. Passes are filed as sibling issues and cross-linked here.

## Cross-cutting rules Drew set

- Auto-resolution is the default; a specific flag overrides it. Defaults: the service's standard port on localhost or its socket.
- Endpoints can be customized per subprogram: a service may have a standard port, a website port, a homepage path, or a unique-ID custom path taken from settings, used raw.
- Everything exposed as a command should also be exposable as MCP and as REST (flag-gated, not all on at once). Later possibly GraphQL by the same switch.

Part of the fleet-surface design mill (Drew, 2026-11-14). Parent issue cross-links all passes.

## What to do

1. **Upstream merges**: merge all upstream commits into each fork (developing-today-forks/opencode and developing-today-forks/openchamber) and ensure both still build and work together with the fleet's config and routing.
2. **Feature-gap analysis**: a feature-gap track between upstream OpenCode and upstream OpenChamber and our forks — upstream has released a mobile app and several other features (the mobile app was a big draw of OpenChamber for Drew). Separately and later: investigate exposing OpenCode and OpenChamber inside ID (not just as an mcpx proxy — iroh + SSH-proxy pre-rendered output, web frontend proxying, their tunnel support: their own cloud tunnel, Tailscale, etc.).

We maintain this code anyway — review each removed feature and decide for ourselves: restore and keep, or accept the removal. Drew likes some of those features and is not ready to lose them by default. (No equivalent removal is known for OpenCode — verify rather than assume.)

## What

v1.1 of the OpenChamber dispatch system (design:
`files/openchamber-dispatch-babysitter-design-2026-10-26.md`): turn
the report-only babysitter into the working dispatcher + babysitter.

## Scope

- **Dispatcher:** claims queue tasks whose packet carries
  `executor: openchamber` (larger code work: effort/m+l, session-shaped
  per triage), admits against (a) location capacity and (b) the POOL
  MAP measurement gate for the routed pool (fresh quota read; ≥85% of
  window = no new heavy work). Creates the session in a per-task
  worktree on branch `queue/<task-id>-<issue>-<slug>` and records the
  binding (session id, location, pool/route, started-at) on the task.
- **Hand-back:** no slot or no headroom → park the task with reason
  class `executor-saturated` and note it on the issue. Saturation is
  reported, never a silent backlog; a Claude lane can still claim the
  task if urgent.
- **Babysitter actions:** stall nudge (one message into a session idle
  >20 min while claiming work: checkpoint/continue/state blocker; max
  2, then escalate to the monitor tracker); wall handling (quota stop =
  park blocked with the wall named, never a PAYG fallback); harvesting
  (session done → verify against GitHub → complete/park/block the task
  with labels synced and an agent-note on the issue).
- **Routing policy as config:** Fast / Workhorse (default) / Frontier
  tiers per the design; escalation to Frontier requires recorded
  evidence (failed Workhorse attempt or design-shap

<!-- agent-note:v1 agent=archer lane=lane-br state=follow-up -->

## Evidence

On `origin/main` (`87e0133554`, 2026-11-15), [`bin/openchamber-start.sh`](https://github.com/developing-today/code/blob/87e0133554/bin/openchamber-start.sh) declares/uses only a single positional argument (the OpenChamber serve script path, passed by the home-manager unit shim):

- `serve="$1"` (line 23)
- empty check: `if [ -z "$serve" ]; then ... exit 1; fi` (lines 24-27)
- it then reads the standing OpenCode server state/password from `~/.local/state/opencode/service-prod.json`, exports credentials, and `exec "$serve"` (lines 29-41)

There is no `$#`/extra-argument validation, so any additional positional arguments after the required serve script are silently ignored before sensitive startup work.

### Repro (safe, no service started)

Using a throwaway executable that exits immediately as the serve script argument:

```bash
tmp=$(mktemp /home/user/.local/share/opencode/tmp/opencode/oc-serve.XXXXXX.sh)
printf '#!/bin/sh\nexit 0\n' > "$tmp" && chmod +x "$tmp"
bash bin/openchamber-start.sh "$tmp" extra-bogus-arg; echo "rc=$?"
rm -f "$tmp"
```

Observed on this host (with `~/.local/state/opencode/service-prod.json` readable): exit code `0` and the dummy serve script was exec'd, proving `extra-bogus-arg` was ignored and the script proceeded through state/password handling and exec.

## Why it matters

`bin/openchamber-start.sh` is an operator/startup wrapper that reads a local password/state file and exports `OPENCODE_PASSWORD` before attaching/starting OpenChambe

## Problem

Tracking issue: dezren39/nix#1117 (cross-repo set — the defect was filed there; the systemd model it names lives in this repo, `home/common/default.nix`. The launchd port in dezren39/nix disables self-handoff for the same failure class.)

The `openchamber` user unit is socket-activated (`openchamber.socket` owns `127.0.0.1:3000`) with `KillMode=process`, so a stop terminates only the tracked main process. On 2026-10-29 the 12:36:40 CDT stop left the actual web server (pid 272664, started 05:22 CDT) running in the cgroup — systemd's own journal: `Unit process 272664 (MainThread) remains running after unit stopped`, with the tracked main an adopted process `not our child`. Socket activation started a new server (pid 1668515) at 12:38:44 and handed it the **same** listen socket (both processes hold fd 3 → socket inode 11096). Both `accept()` on it, so `/api/version` answers alternate `startedAt` 10:22:55Z / 17:38:45Z under one serverId and `/api/session-activity` flips between divergent session sets. Fleet dispatch/capacity reads over port 3000 are unreliable while this lasts.

- `openchamber-serve` (the start script) now reaps leftover servers before `exec`: SIGTERM, up to 10 s drain (OpenChamber's documented SIGTERM drain), then SIGKILL. Because the start script's store path is the unit's deploy key, this change also triggers the activation restart that deploys it.
- The matcher requires a `node`/`openchamber` exe **plus** the `serve --port 3000` cmdline —

Refs #2174 (Gap 1 of the evidence gaps; Gap 3 named as the follow-on on the issue).

Builds the per-run history consumer for OpenChamber scheduled tasks in pm-stack/scheduled-history/:

- Design: a polling reconciler, not an event consumer — the scheduled-task-ran events are ephemeral and report enqueue/send rather than completion (recon on #2174), so each tick polls `openchamber schedule list --json` and reconciles runs keyed by (task id, lastScheduledFor): exactly one durable row per run; outcome follows the record until terminal, then the row freezes; a newer run finalizes an older non-terminal row as superseded.
- Store: ~/.local/state/openchamber-scheduled-history/history.json (atomic tmp+rename), rows carry task id/name, project, scheduled/start/finish, scheduler duration, session id, outcome + terminal flag, and token/cost totals enriched from the OpenCode session store (session_v2, the #2072 source) by session id — null when absent, never invented.
- Read path: `collect.py list [--task] [--since] [--until] [--json]` — the input the #2174 comparison and the Gap 3 watchdog will consume.
- Deployment: user systemd service+timer (5-minute tick) mirroring opencode-usage-export; installed and enabled on the laptop. The installed unit temporarily ExecStarts from this branch's worktree; reinstall from the primary clone after merge (the repo unit already carries the canonical ~/git/code path). No existing cron job, scheduled task, cadence, or lane count is changed.

Live verif

## Summary

The single-instance guard added to the generated `openchamber-serve` wrapper (bc6044f, for dezren39/nix#1117) never matches a running server, so it is a no-op in production: after a restart, a leftover OpenChamber server keeps sharing the socket-activated listener on 127.0.0.1:3000 with the new instance.

## Root cause

In the wrapper as generated into the Nix store, the guard's cmdline capture is:

```
cmd="$(cat "$proc/cmdline" 2>/dev/null | tr '\\0' ' ')"
```

The generated script literally contains `tr '\\0' ' '` (verified byte-for-byte with `grep | cat -A` on the store file). In shell single quotes that passes backslash + backslash + `0` to `tr`, and GNU tr reads `\\` as an escaped backslash, so the translate set is {backslash, `0`} — NUL bytes are never converted to spaces. Bash command substitution then strips the NULs, concatenating the argv words (`...cli.jsserve--foreground--port3000--host...`), so neither the `cli.js serve` pattern nor the `--port 3000 ` boundary pattern can ever match any real process.

Intended text in the generated script: `tr '\0' ' '`.

## Observed impact (2026-10-29 23:50 CDT, laptop)

`systemctl --user restart openchamber.service` with the guarded wrapper: the tracked main (pid 3892827) stopped cleanly, the new instance (pid 483540) started, the guard logged no reap, and the untracked leftover (pid 1668515, started 12:38 CDT) was still holding fd 3 on 127.0.0.1:3000 alongside the new instance (`ss -tlnp` showed both pids). Replay
title: openchamber-serve single-instance guard never matches: generated wrapper has tr '\\0' instead of tr '\0'

Update the fleet-watchdog roster to the merged job id. Keep the measurement gate binding: no dispatch without a quota picture ≤60 min old covering all pools.

## Finding

The stale-branch cleanup workflow deletes candidates in a bare loop under `set -euo pipefail`, with no per-branch failure handling. One failed `git push origin --delete` aborts the whole run: later candidates are never attempted, the finish line never prints, and the same undeletable branch (ruleset protection, a concurrent delete, a transient push error) can starve every later candidate on every subsequent daily live run.

This is one cross-repo set — the workflow is byte-identical in the three repos below; file/fix it as a set, not per-repo duplicates.

## Evidence

- Source PRs (this repo): PR #1464 created the workflow; PR #1493 (`ci: run branch cleanup daily`, head `494e6dd5`) changed the schedule to daily, and its body states `BRANCH_CLEANUP_LIVE` has been set to true and verified — so scheduled runs perform live deletions daily.
- Current main `b2adaf47` (developing-today/code), `.github/workflows/branch-cleanup.yml`: `set -euo pipefail` at line 46; deletion loop at lines 150–159 with a bare `git push origin --delete "$branch"` at line 155 and no guard, failure collection, or `|| true`.
- Same loop, verified on current main today: developing-today/opencode (`9ba2221f`, workflow lines 46 and 155) and developing-today/openchamber (`93027f59`, lines 46 and 155).
- Mechanism: under `set -e`, a failing command in the loop body (not in a condition) terminates the script immediately — later loop iterations never run. This exact mechanism was reproduced and confirm
title: branch-cleanup: one failed 'git push origin --delete' aborts the live daily run — same unguarded loop in code, opencode, openchamber

## What

- **System env**: compose the Android SDK from nixpkgs' `androidenv` (cmdline-tools, platform-tools, build-tools 35.0.0, platforms;android-35 — no emulator/sources/system-images) and install it with `jdk21` in `nixos/environment`, exporting `ANDROID_HOME`/`ANDROID_SDK_ROOT`/`JAVA_HOME`.
- **Dev shells**: the same SDK + JDK 21 in `nix-common.nix` (shared by `nix-shell` and `nix develop`), with the env exports in the shared `shellHook`.
- **License**: `android_sdk.accept_license = true` on the system pkgs (`nixos/nixpkgs/default.nix`) and on both dev-shell pkgs imports. `nixpkgs.config` is a no-op because the system assigns `nixpkgs.pkgs` directly.
- **Signing key**: the OpenChamber Android release keystore + passwords, sops-encrypted to the laptop-framework age key under `secrets/sops/groups/admin/openchamber-android.yaml`. The same values are set as repository secrets on `developing-today/openchamber`.

## Why

`packages/mobile/scripts/with-mobile-env.mjs` reads `ANDROID_HOME`/`JAVA_HOME` but falls back to macOS Homebrew paths, so Android builds break on Linux without both exported.

## Verification

- `nix develop --command bash -c '...'` and `nix-shell --run '...' ./shell.nix` both resolve `java`, `sdkmanager`, `adb`, `bun`.
- `assembleRelease` for OpenChamber produced an APK signed with the stored certificate (SHA-256 `9f01e729…`).
- `sops -d` of the new secret returns the exact keystore (4370 bytes, SHA-256 `5312c41f…`) and passwords.

## Problem

`pm-stack/opencode-claimant/install.mjs` — the installer that writes the #3026 claimant scheduled task into the laptop's real OpenChamber project store — performs **no argument validation**. `main()` (install.mjs:65-71) collects only the spellings it knows:


PR #357 (https://github.com/developing-today/code/pull/357, commit 55efb43d, merged in 238adf46) split `jules.yml`'s shared workflow-level concurrency group into per-job groups "keyed by its target" (its words) — but the new `manual` job's group is a constant, and it is the one job whose target varies on every run: the dispatch `prompt`. The same constant-group-over-varying-inputs pattern also sits in four sibling Jules workflows across three repos (listed below); none of them sets `queue:`, so GitHub's default `queue: single` semantics apply.
